name: Urticaria & angioedema
general: Find and avoid triggers (NSAIDs, foods only if clearly linked, infections). Acute: usually no tests. Chronic (>6 weeks): CBC, ESR/CRP; thyroid antibodies if indicated. Score with UAS7, control with UCT. Angioedema without wheals: check for ACE inhibitor, C4 (hereditary).
special: Anaphylaxis/laryngeal angioedema: Inj. adrenaline 0.5 mg IM (1:1000) and emergency care. Pregnancy: loratadine/cetirizine preferred.

rx.drug: Tab. Levocetirizine 5 mg / Fexofenadine 180 mg / Bilastine 20 mg
Severe acute flare: Tab. Prednisolone 20 mg

rx.instr: Observe 2 h after dose; can increase to 600 mg / every 2 weeks
If omalizumab not available or not effective; BP, creatinine
